market.coverage: Market CTR / CVR read by the syntax-week view over 2026-08-26 → 2026-09-30; 3 published SQP weeks inside it (2026-08-30 → 2026-09-19).

notInMatrix.realAcos: Real ACOS (waste-adjusted) has no field in the metric matrix at syntax grain yet.
notInMatrix.clickShare: SQP click share has no field in the metric matrix at syntax grain yet.
notInMatrix.placementUnits: Units at placement are an ESTIMATE built from two: the estimated clicks there (a dense fold) times the estimated units-per-click, which is an index on this row's own rate in the CVR's construction. A direct split is impossible — units appear in only 711 of 2,564 Top-of-Search campaign-placement cells, the SAME 711 that carry sales. On this account units and orders are near-identical (8,653 of 8,803 cells have them equal, 1.03 units per order), so this tracks clicks x the estimated CVR closely; it is here because units are the unit you act on.
notInMatrix.placementOffRate: Off Amazon is withheld from the estimated CTR, CVR and ACOS by the ruling of 2026-08-30: of 117 campaigns with an Off Amazon placement row, 101 had ZERO orders there, and it recorded sales in 52 of 603 placement cells. Rendered as a number it would read as a claim about how Off Amazon converts, which the data cannot support either way. Its impressions, clicks, spend and CPC are shown — those legs are well evidenced.

contract: syntax x day: segments are FACETS, not a partition — a term counts in every group it matches, so segment rows over-sum the product

searchVolume.note: Search Volume is the keyword library's figure, not a measurement over the selected days — it does not move when the date range does. At segment level it sums every MKL keyword the segment claims, each once; at keyword level it is that term's own figure. The two do not reconcile: a segment claims thousands of library keywords, while the rows beneath it are only the terms that took ad traffic in this window.
searchVolume.unitWarning: The volumes come from a first-non-zero vendor cascade that reconciles no units — an sqp figure is a WEEKLY true count and a helium10 / asinsight / datadive one is a MONTHLY estimate. Hover any cell for its own source. Read the column as a size ORDER, not a count.

notes: Every rate is BLENDED — the window's total over its total (spend over sales, clicks over impressions) — never the mean of daily or per-row rates.

Sales, orders and every rate built on them carry 7-day attribution: the trailing seven days are still filling in and read LOW. The newest day is also a partial day. Compare settled windows with settled windows.

A search term counts in EVERY group it matches, so group rows overlap and their spend shares over-sum 100% on purpose. They cannot be added or subtracted; use ppc_summary for the product total. TACoS does not exist at group grain.
